name: Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma)

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence and more severe disease in Black Americans
Choctaw Native Americans have highest prevalence reported worldwide
More common in women (F:M approximately 4:1 to 9:1)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: 2013 ACR/EULAR Classification Criteria for Systemic Sclerosis

criteria.description: Skin thickening of the fingers of both hands extending proximal to the MCPs (sufficient criterion, score 9)
Skin thickening of the fingers: puffy fingers (score 2) or sclerodactyly distal to MCPs (score 4)
Fingertip lesions: digital tip ulcers (score 2) or fingertip pitting scars (score 3)
Pulmonary arterial hypertension and/or interstitial lung disease (score 2)
SSc-related autoantibodies: anti-centromere, anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I), or anti-RNA polymerase III (score 3)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Total score >= 9 classifies as SSc. Skin thickening proximal to MCPs is a sufficient criterion alone (9 points). Otherwise, sum individual item scores (higher of sub-items counts).
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Two major subsets: limited cutaneous SSc (lcSSc, skin involvement distal to elbows/knees, face) and diffuse cutaneous SSc (dcSSc, proximal skin involvement). CREST = Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia.

pathognomonic.notes: Begins in fingers; may progress proximally in diffuse type
Often the first symptom; may precede other manifestations by years

common.notes: Reduced distal esophageal peristalsis and lower esophageal sphincter tone
NSIP pattern most common; more frequent in dcSSc with anti-Scl-70

occasional.notes: More common in lcSSc with anti-centromere; leading cause of death
Subcutaneous calcium deposits; painful and prone to infection
Palpable crepitus over tendons; associated with diffuse disease

rare.notes: Acute hypertension, AKI, MAHA; more common in dcSSc and anti-RNA polymerase III
searchTerms: sudden kidney failure with high blood pressure

rare.symptomName: Gastric antral vascular ectasia (GAVE / watermelon stomach)
searchTerms: stomach blood vessel dilation causing bleeding

laboratory: ANA positive (>95%, often nucleolar or centromere pattern)
Anti-Scl-70 / anti-topoisomerase I (dcSSc, associated with ILD)
Anti-RNA polymerase III (dcSSc, associated with renal crisis and cancer risk)
Elevated ESR; may have elevated CRP
imaging: High-resolution CT chest: ground-glass opacities, fibrosis (NSIP or UIP pattern)
Echocardiography: estimated RVSP for PAH screening
Nailfold capillaroscopy: dilated capillaries, avascular areas, microhemorrhages
Hand radiographs: calcinosis, acro-osteolysis, soft tissue atrophy
genetic: No single causative gene; polygenic susceptibility
HLA-DRB1 associations vary by antibody subtype
IRF5, STAT4, CD247, and other immune-related polymorphisms
other: Modified Rodnan Skin Score (mRSS) for skin involvement
Pulmonary function tests: reduced FVC and DLCO
Annual screening for PAH (echocardiography + PFTs + biomarkers)

distinguishingFeatures: MCTD has high-titer anti-U1 RNP antibodies
MCTD has features of SLE, SSc, and myositis overlapping
MCTD generally has milder skin fibrosis
DM has proximal muscle weakness as primary feature
DM has heliotrope rash and Gottron's papules
hEDS has skin laxity not skin tightening
hEDS has joint hypermobility not contractures

redFlags: Rapid skin thickening progression (risk for renal crisis in dcSSc)
New hypertension or rising creatinine (scleroderma renal crisis - emergency)
Progressive dyspnea (ILD progression or new PAH)
Anti-RNA polymerase III positivity (cancer screening recommended)
New pericardial effusion or arrhythmia (cardiac involvement)
references: van den Hoogen F, et al. 2013 classification criteria for systemic sclerosis: an American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism collaborative initiative. Arthritis Rheum. 2013;65(11):2737-47.
Denton CP, Khanna D. Systemic sclerosis. Lancet. 2017;390(10103):1685-99.
Allanore Y, et al. Systemic sclerosis. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2015;1:15002.
Kowal-Bielecka O, et al. Update of EULAR recommendations for the treatment of systemic sclerosis. Ann Rheum Dis. 2017;76(8):1327-39.
